info.name: ShopTrace API
info.description:
# ShopTrace API

Every route on the server, with real Ghanaian test data already filled in. Tokens and ids are captured automatically, so you never copy-paste an id.

## Before you run anything

1. **Start the API** — `npm run dev` (port 4000).
2. **Create the first admin** — registration can no longer grant the admin role, so run:

   ```
   npm run seed:admin -- "ShopTrace Admin" admin@shoptrace.com 0244000000 admin12345
   ```

3. **Select the `ShopTrace Local` environment** (top right).
4. **Add `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_local_only` to your `server/.env`** and restart. It must match `paystackSecret` in the environment, or every webhook request returns 500. It does NOT have to be a real Paystack key for the webhook tests.

## How to use it

Run the folders **in order, top to bottom**. The order is a real dependency chain: you cannot list a product until a shop is verified, and a merchant cannot see an order until it is paid.

- Requests marked **★** are the ones that prove something important. Do not skip them.
- Requests marked **✗** are meant to FAIL. A red status is the pass condition, and each one has a test asserting the exact code.
- Open the **Test results** tab after each request. Every request carries assertions, so you get a pass/fail rather than having to read the JSON yourself.
- The first request, **Health check**, sets a fresh `runId` so every email is unique. Re-run it before re-running the whole collection.

## What cannot be fully tested yet

| Needs | Effect if missing |
| --- | --- |
| `CLOUDINARY_URL` | Upload routes return 503 |
| A real `sk_test_` Paystack key | Initiate/verify/refund return 502; signed webhooks still work |
| `REDIS_URL` (Upstash) | Job queueing returns 503; use the manual expiry sweep |

item.name: 07 · Payments
item.description: **Set `paystackSecret` in the environment to the same value as `PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY` in your `.env` first** — otherwise every webhook returns 500. The signed-webhook requests build and sign their own body in a pre-request script, so they work with no Paystack account at all.

request.description: Anyone on the internet can reach this URL. Without a signature check they could mark any order paid just by knowing its number.
A correctly-built body with one character changed in the signature.

exec: // Paystack signs the EXACT bytes of the body. So the body is built here,
// stored in a variable, and the request body is just that variable -
// which means what we sign is byte-for-byte what gets sent.
if (!secret) { throw new Error("Set paystackSecret in the environment"); }

request.description: A PERFECTLY SIGNED event that claims only 1% of the real amount. A signature proves the message came from Paystack — it does not prove the customer paid enough. Returns 200 (the event was received) but the order must stay unpaid.
